A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same few-shot label-unlearning work in vertical federated learning, despite substantial revisions and a new title. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments on four datasets, including accuracy, membership-inference attacks, runtime, privacy-defense evaluations, and an appendix passive-model-completion attack.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on seven datasets, including revised unlearning results, component ablations, scalability measurements, and deletion-membership leakage results.

M1.justification: v2 adds a retained-accuracy recovery stage that performs gradient descent on mixed retained-data embeddings after label forgetting (Section 4.3, Algorithm 1). It also moves mixup generation from passive parties to the active party, explicitly coordinating the mixing coefficient. These change the optimization and communication procedure beyond the original mixup-plus-ascent method.

E1.justification: v2 adds Brain Tumor MRI, COVID-19 Radiography, and Yahoo Answers evaluations, extending coverage to medical imaging and text classification. The original MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ModelNet coverage and single-, two-, and four-label unlearning scenarios remain.

E2.justification: The principal comparison set is retained, with SSD added to accuracy, ASR, and runtime comparisons. GA results from v1 Figure 11 are absent from the corresponding v2 ASR tables, although GA remains in ablations. Retraining is also omitted from v2's runtime plot, whereas it appeared in v1 Figure 5.

E3.justification: Previously stated settings change: ResNet18/CIFAR10 single-label unlearning increases from 15 to 20 epochs, and multi-label batch size changes from 32 to 64, alongside other learning-rate and epoch revisions (v1 Tables 6–7; v2 Tables 9–10). Scalability evaluation extends to eight passive parties. v2 also introduces deletion-membership leakage averaged across classes and a MixText protocol for text evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 extends the original data-size ablation to isolate mixup and recovery, adds mixing-coefficient sensitivity and deletion-membership leakage analyses, and expands participant-count testing. The original boundary-leakage and privacy-defense analyses are retained in the appendix. However, the passive-model-completion attack in v1 Figure 10 and Appendix A.2 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random trials and mean/standard-deviation reporting. v2 newly supplies standard deviations for ASR results previously displayed without uncertainty in v1's bar charts. Conversely, participant-count accuracy results move from v1 Table 4 with standard deviations to v2 Figure 4 without displayed uncertainty.

E6.justification: Many proposed-method results are replaced: Table 1 retained accuracy changes from 67.85% to 69.96% for ResNet18/CIFAR100 and from 83.32% to 87.69% for ModelNet, accompanying method/settings changes rather than controlled same-setting gains. Amnesiac's CIFAR100 ASR changes from 96.1% in v1 Figures 4/11 to 2.60% in v2 Table 1. New datasets, SSD, and leakage evaluations add substantial results; v2 Table 6 reports 14.38%/4.04% leakage versus retraining's 100%.

T1.justification: v1 contains objectives and update equations but no corresponding theorem or proof. v2 adds a gradient-alignment theorem and a two-layer linear/MSE derivation (Section 4.2, Appendix A.1), concentration arguments using Chebyshev and Bernstein inequalities, and a KL-divergence definition of process privacy (Section 5.4). These are substantive theoretical additions; a tight process-privacy bound remains explicitly unresolved.

C1.justification: The first-VFL-label-unlearning claim remains, but the proposed contribution changes from forgetting with a few disclosed private labels to a public-data framework with explicit retained-accuracy recovery. The abstract and introduction now claim effectiveness across image and text modalities and make utility preservation central to the approach, materially extending the original contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of recovery, mixup variance reduction, and why very low ASR may indicate the Streisand effect. Appendix A.9 identifies limitations involving unsuitable public data, asynchronous operation, and repeated deletion requests. Section 5.4 distinguishes its process-privacy concept from the still-open problem of deriving tight bounds.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, A100 hardware disclosure, explicit mixing coefficients and target-label identities, recovery hyperparameters, expanded baseline implementation descriptions, and image/text partitioning instructions. Appendix A.8 also documents MixText architecture and Yahoo Answers sample counts. Some earlier information is lost, including the precise ModelNet training/test counts stated in v1 Appendix A.1.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against zero-shot and few-shot unlearning, newer vertical-unlearning work, and few-shot mixup literature. Appendix A.7/Table 8 introduces a systematic comparison of federated-unlearning targets and privacy protection, asserting distinctive protection during deletion; Section 5.4 adds a process-privacy novelty claim. Publication updates to retained references, such as SecureCut, are not new works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related-work organization, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. The original leakage-focused Section 3 becomes background, with leakage discussion redistributed to Section 5.4 and Appendix A.3. The appendix is reorganized into nine thematic sections, with substantial explanatory expansion and terminology changes from classes to labels.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the framework diagram, replaces the runtime bar chart with participant-count curves, and integrates ASR into expanded accuracy tables. It redesigns participant-count displays, combines and relocates privacy-defense plots, removes the PMC figure, and adds notation, related-work, leakage, and sensitivity tables plus feature-partition illustrations. These substantially change presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the support for utility preservation through an explicit recovery stage and a component ablation: Figure 3 reports retained accuracy of 88.11% without recovery versus 89.29% with it, while forgotten-label accuracy remains zero. Broader evaluation, implementation disclosures, and concrete limitations also help. These gains are tempered by removal of the passive-model-completion attack and privacy-guarantee framing that exceeds the demonstrated theory: Section 5.4 leaves tight privacy bounds open. The net improvement is clearer empirical support and documentation, not an established privacy guarantee.
